expectation: Cytoplasmic, granular signal in neutrophils (and some monocytes). These are scattered single cells, more common in some tumours than others, sometimes dense near necrosis or in inflamed stroma. They should sit among nuclei, not light every cell, and their numbers should vary between images.
observed: A: discrete yellow dots in most images, dense in images 2–3 (row 1) and sparse in others. Their density varies independently of nuclear density. B, C: scattered compact cytoplasmic blobs about one cell wide beside nuclei, with most cells unstained. D: a few granular blobs around nuclei.
why: A distinct, sparse population of cells with granular cytoplasmic signal varies in density between images and does not follow nuclear density, as a neutrophil stain should.
notes: MPO marks scattered compact cytoplasmic blobs that sit beside nuclei, with most cells negative. Their abundance varies strongly between images, which fits neutrophil infiltration rather than haze or autofluorescence.
